Justice Raveendran said he was “shocked” by the suggestion, though he acknowledged that it reflected the frustration caused by the present state of challenges to arbitral awards. “ Imagine, out of desperation, Justice Nariman said, let us have a first one appeal, full appeal and be done with it. The entire purpose of arbitration is to have finality .” Justice RV Raveendran Justice Raveendran said that if courts were given wider appellate powers, including the ability to extensively reconsider or modify awards, the distinction between arbitration and ordinary litigation would begin to disappear. He was speaking at a panel discussion titled “A Judge’s wish list of what the law ought to be” on the concluding day of GHAC Arbitration Week 2026 in Gandhinagar. The three-day conference, held from September 4 to 6 at GIFT City Club, was organised by the Gujarat High Court in collaboration with the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre. Senior Advocate Saurabh Soparkar moderated the discussion. Justice Raveendran also raised concerns over inconsistent Supreme Court rulings on arbitration. He said “ We have 37 judges. The firm is led by Faizur Rehman as Managing Partner, together with Partners Sukanya Lal , Tushar Srivastava , Waseem Anwar , Sachin Nagendra Sharma and Amit K. Pateria . The team brings together experience from corporate legal advisory, commercial litigation, arbitration and regulatory context. Niyama’s lawyers have experience in advising and representing businesses, institutions, public sector entities and other organisations on transactional, regulatory and contentious matters. The Firm will operate as a Partner-led practice, with senior lawyers remaining closely involved in client mandates. Niyama has been structured around the understanding that legal issues increasingly cut across conventional practice boundaries. A transaction may carry regulatory and governance implications; an infrastructure project may involve contracting, policy and dispute-related questions; and businesses operating in regulated sectors often require advice that brings several areas of law together. items.title: Uttar Pradesh government orders probe into RPNLUP Assistant Professor recruitment
items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has ordered a probe into the recruitment of 12 Assistant Professors at Dr Rajendra Prasad National Law University, Prayagraj (RPNLUP). The order was issued by Dinesh Singh, Special Secretary of the Justice Department. The committee comprises the Principal Secretaries of three State departments. It will be headed by M Devraj, Principal Secretary, Personnel and Appointments Department. MP Agarwal, Principal Secretary, Higher Education Department, and Uday Pratap Singh, Principal Secretary, Justice and Legal Advisory Department are the other two members. The committee has been directed to submit its findings within 30 days. RPNLUP had advertised 12 Assistant Professor (Law) posts in March this year. Interviews for the posts were held between July 22 and 30. According to a report , the State of Uttar Pradesh's Additional Law Remembrancer, also a member of the University's Executive Council (EC), had sought records and explanations from the University's Registrar on the recruitment process. In that letter, he allegedly mentioned that complete information regarding the appointments was not placed before the EC during its meeting on July 31, because of which he and another EC member abstained from voting on the appointments. The report said that the Additional Law Remembrancer asked whether shortlisting and selection committee formation adhered to University Grants Commission (UGC) regulations, and whether an academic-score chart in the prescribed format was prepared. Separately, a complaint reportedly to the Chief Minister alleged that that three of the Vice Chancellor's (VC) former students were among those selected during the process. Another complaint, addressed to the UGC Chairman and copied to Bar & Bench , also sought a stay on one candidate's appointment and an independent inquiry, alleging the candidate's joining was permitted without the Registrar's signature. Following this, RPNLUP on August 20 issued a press note calling coverage of the appointments defamatory . [Read Order]

items.title: Delhi court sends Swatantra Bhardwaj to judicial custody for a day in Jantar Mantar assault case
items.summary: A Delhi court on Sunday sent right-wing influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj to judicial custody (JC) for a day in the case related to alleged assault on the father of a Dalit student-activist during the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protests at Jantar Mantar in July. Duty Magistrate Anjali Singh of the Patiala House Court passed the order. According to a lawyer involved in the case, Bhardwaj was produced at the judge's residence through virtual conference (VC). Police asked him to be sent to JC for 14 days. However, since he was produced before the Duty Magistrate, Bhardwaj was sent to JC for a day. The request for additional custody will be decided by the concerned court on Monday. Bhardwaj was arrested from Uttar Pradesh yesterday. He has been booked for offence of assault and provisions under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act [SC/ST Act] and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act). Bhardwaj was initially booked only for the offences under Sections 115(2) (causing simple hurt) and 126(2) (wrongful restraint) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). He later took to social media and claimed that had cracked the skull of the girl's father and was detained by the police only for a few hours. He also claimed proximity to NDA leaders Kapil Mishra and Chirag Paswan. Paswan denied the same and also lodged a separate complaint against Bhardwaj for misusing his name. Meanwhile, after Cockroach Janta Party leaders along with the girl and her father protested at the Parliament Street police station, more serious charges were added.

items.title: ‘Naanu Gauri’: Remembering Gauri Lankesh through a debate on campus dissent
items.summary: Nine years after an assassin tried to silence journalist Gauri Lankesh, the All India Students' Association (AISA), the student wing of the CPI(ML) Liberation, held a panel discussion titled ‘Campuses to Streets: Is Democracy Under Siege?’ in Bengaluru on September 5, marking the 9th anniversary of the journalist-activist’s assassination. Nine years after her killing, the case continues at what critics have described as a painfully slow pace. The organisers opened the event with the call “Naanu Gauri”, meaning “I am Gauri”, urging people not simply to grieve her death but to carry forward the memories and ideas she stood for. The panel featured Jawaharlal Nehru University Students' Union (JNUSU) Joint Secretary and AISA leader Danish Ali, who has been active in student politics since 2019 and was among the hunger strikers at Jantar Mantar; sociologist and author Lakshmipathi CG, who writes extensively on caste; and writer-activist Meena Kandasamy, known for her poetry on Dalit and feminist resistance. The three speakers also released a booklet curated by AISA Karnataka on the state of public education in India, with a focus on schools and universities in Karnataka. The booklet describes the National Education Policy (NEP) as “a dangerous intersection of neoliberalism and saffronisation” that reshapes education in the interests of capital, caste and ideological control. Danish recalled hearing about Gauri's murder as a school student in 2017. She said the killing made her question India's claim to being a democracy, questions that, she said, remain unanswered nine years later and ultimately pushed her towards student politics. Danish said dissent on campuses across India continues to be met with rustication, fines and police cases. She was among the JNUSU members fined Rs 20,000 each after protesting a surveillance system that the university sought to introduce. The university also imposed a fine of Rs 19,000 on each student who was not directly involved in the protest. “The JNU administration shamelessly fined them for attending, clapping and sloganeering at the protest site,” she said. She said this year's movement against the leak of NEET question papers began online, as people started “rejecting their whole politics of labelling”. She said the movement grew from social media into street protests at Jantar Mantar and in various parts of the country, which she claimed eventually forced the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
